Folks — forwarding ProcureCo's asks. Quick notes and proposed attachments: redwood_privacy_snippet_v1.docx (two alternative public snippets) and subprocessor_list_202806.csv (current list + regions).

Short answers up-front:
- Data processing location: Hosted API is region-configurable; customer requests can be scoped to our US, EU, or APAC clusters depending on plan. We do not export customer prompts for model training by default for enterprise customers on Dedicated/Private; for Hosted API, we offer an opt-out and can provide contract language.
- Subprocessor regional restrictions: We maintain a subprocessor mapping per region. For EU-only residency we can offer contractual commitments on where primary processing occurs and limit subprocessor access accordingly, though some infra support vendors may still be US-based — see attached CSV for items that require additional contract controls (e.g., monitoring, billing).
- Audit logs & DPA appendix: we have an audit log anchor in the DPA (see page 3, section 2.1 in the doc link). I pulled the one-pager and added a plain-language blurb.

Action items:
- @Kimberly: Can you confirm the standard Hosted API default for model improvement opt-out language and whether we can push a stronger EU-only subprocessor clause for this deal?
- @Marcus: Please check whether the two infra vendors listed in the CSV (TelemetryOps Inc., MetricsCloud) are permissible to mark as "restricted" under the EU residency toggle.
- @Laura: If the attached snippet looks right, can you send a version with two tone variants (legal-lite and sales-friendly) back to Sara?

Thanks — I'll wait for internal signoff before we send the updated snippet.

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Solutions & GTM Privacy
Redwood Inference

Hi Sara / Alex — thanks for the questions. Below is a short, consumer-friendly one-liner and a 2-sentence paragraph you can drop into procurement/ SOWs. I also listed the contract language we can commit to for EU residency.

One-liner (sales-friendly):
"Redwood processes customer data in the region you select (US, EU, or APAC) and does not use customer prompts for model training unless you opt in."

Two-sentence consumer paragraph (legal-lite):
"We process and store data in the region you choose for your deployment. For Hosted API customers, Redwood does not include customer prompts or outputs in model-improvement training unless the customer explicitly opts in via contract or console setting; for enterprise residency commitments, we will contractually restrict processing and limit subprocessor access to the selected region where technically feasible."

Contract commitments we can offer for EU-only residency:
- Primary processing and storage in EU region (specific clusters identified in DPA appendix).
- Subprocessor access controls: Redwood will only engage subprocessors that have agreed to EU data handling terms; two infra support vendors that require US-based tooling can be restricted from handling customer content for this account by adding an exhibit to the DPA.
- Audit support: annual SOC snapshot and on-demand audit log export for the account under NDA.

Attachments: I attached a Drive link with the DPA appendix and sample signature page for EU-only residency: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-redwood-privacy-draft

If that works, can you confirm which variant (one-liner or paragraph) procurement prefers and whether we should include the two infra vendors in the restricted list? Once confirmed, we'll send a final DocuSign-ready DPA exhibit.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Manager, Product Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
